segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then the whole assembly of them rose and led him to Pilate.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They began to accuse him, saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “We found this man subverting our nation, forbidding the payment of taxes to Caesar, and saying that he himself is the Messiah, a king.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Pilate asked him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Are you the king of the Jews?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He answered him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “You say so.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Pilate said to the chief priests and the crowds,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “I find no ground for a charge against this man.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But they kept insisting,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “He stirs up the people, teaching throughout all Judea, starting from Galilee and reaching as far as here.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When Pilate heard this, he asked whether the man was a Galilean,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and on learning that he was under Herod’s jurisdiction, he sent him over to Herod, who was himself also in Jerusalem in those days.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When Herod saw Jesus he was very glad, for he had been wanting to see him for a long time because of what he had heard about him, and he was hoping to see some sign done by him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He questioned him at length, but Jesus gave him no answer.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The chief priests and the scribes stood there, accusing him vehemently.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Herod too, with his troops, treated him with contempt and mocked him; then he dressed him in a splendid robe and sent him back to Pilate.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: That same day Herod and Pilate became friends with each other, for before this they had been enemies.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Pilate called together the chief priests, the rulers, and the people,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and said to them,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “You brought this man to me as someone who was leading the people astray. And look, I examined him in your presence and found in this man no ground for the charges you bring against him.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: Nor did Herod, for he sent him back to us. Look, he has done nothing that deserves death.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: So I will have him disciplined and then release him.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But they all cried out together,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Away with this man! Release Barabbas to us!”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: This was a man who had been thrown into prison because of an uprising that had taken place in the city, and for murder.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Pilate addressed them again, wanting to release Jesus,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: but they kept shouting,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Crucify, crucify him!”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: A third time he said to them,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Why, what evil has this man done? I have found in him no ground for a death sentence. So I will have him disciplined and then release him.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But they pressed him with loud voices, demanding that he be crucified, and their voices prevailed.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So Pilate ruled that their demand should be granted.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He released the man who had been thrown into prison for uprising and murder, the one they were demanding, and he handed Jesus over to their will.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: As they led him away, they seized a certain Simon of Cyrene, who was coming in from the country, and laid the cross on him to carry behind Jesus.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: A great crowd of the people followed him, among them women who were mourning and lamenting him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But Jesus turned to them and said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Daughters of Jerusalem, do not weep for me; weep instead for yourselves and for your children,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: for look, days are coming when they will say, ‘Blessed are the barren, the wombs that never bore and the breasts that never nursed!’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Then they will begin to say to the mountains, ‘Fall on us!’ and to the hills, ‘Cover us!’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For if they do these things when the wood is green, what will happen when it is dry?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Two others, criminals, were also led away to be put to death with him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When they came to the place called the Skull, they crucified him there with the criminals, one on his right and one on his left.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And they cast lots to divide his clothes among themselves.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The people stood watching. The rulers too were sneering at him, saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “He saved others; let him save himself, if this is the Messiah of God, the Chosen One!”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The soldiers also mocked him, coming up and offering him sour wine

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “If you are the king of the Jews, save yourself!”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: There was also an inscription over him: “This is the king of the Jews.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: One of the criminals who were hanging there kept insulting him:

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Are you not the Messiah? Save yourself and us!”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But the other answered, rebuking him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Do you not even fear God, since you are under the same sentence?

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: And we are here justly, for we are getting what our deeds deserve; but this man has done nothing wrong.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then he said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Jesus, remember me when you come into your kingdom.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said to him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Truly I tell you, today you will be with me in paradise.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: It was now about the sixth hour, and darkness came over the whole land until the ninth hour,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: for the sun’s light failed. And the curtain of the sanctuary was torn down the middle.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then Jesus cried out in a loud voice,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Father, into your hands I entrust my spirit.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Having said this, he breathed his last.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When the centurion saw what had happened, he glorified God, saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Truly this man was righteous.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And all the crowds that had gathered for this spectacle, when they saw what had happened, went home beating their breasts.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But all who knew him stood at a distance, along with the women who had followed him from Galilee, watching these things.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now there was a man named Joseph, a member of the council, a good and righteous man—

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: he had not agreed with their decision and their action—from Arimathea, a town of the Jews, who was waiting for the kingdom of God.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: This man went to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then he took it down, wrapped it in a linen cloth, and laid him in a tomb cut in the rock, where no one had yet been laid.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: It was the day of Preparation, and the Sabbath was about to begin.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The women who had come with him from Galilee followed behind and saw the tomb and how his body was laid.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then they went back and prepared spices and perfumed oils. On the Sabbath they rested according to the commandment.

notes.note: The Greek word is the one traditionally rendered “Christ”. Here it is a title, the anointed king Israel expected, and that title is the substance of the charge, so “Messiah” is used, as in several modern translations. The Greek has no article, and the phrase could also be read “an anointed king”.

The Greek word rendered “nation” here, of the Jewish people as a political unit, is the same word that in the plural is usually translated “Gentiles”. English needs two words for what Greek expresses with one.

This is Herod Antipas, son of Herod the Great, who ruled Galilee and Perea under Rome. He was presumably in Jerusalem for Passover. Because Jesus was a Galilean, Pilate could refer the case to him. Only Luke records this hearing.

The verb ordinarily means to bring up, instruct or correct a child. Here it is Pilate’s mild term for a beating given as a warning before release, lighter than the scourging that preceded crucifixion. Many versions spell out the sense as “flog” or generalize it to “punish”; “disciplined” keeps the understatement of the Greek.

notes.phrase: But they all cried out together
notes.note: Verse 17 (“Now he was obliged to release one prisoner to them at the festival”) is absent from the earliest manuscripts and is not in the Greek text translated here. It is generally regarded as a later explanatory addition based on Matthew 27:15 and Mark 15:6.

notes.phrase: “Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing.”
notes.note: This prayer is absent from several early and important manuscripts, including Papyrus 75 and Codex Vaticanus, and present in others. Scholars are divided on whether Luke wrote it or whether it is a very early tradition added to his Gospel.

The Greek verb covers abusive speech against anyone, human or divine, whereas modern English “blaspheme” is confined to irreverence toward God. Here the criminal is taunting Jesus to his face, so “insulting” is used. Modern versions vary among “railed at”, “derided” and “hurled insults at”.

notes.phrase: when you come into your kingdom
notes.note: The Greek text translated here reads literally “in your kingdom”, which can mean either “when you enter your kingdom” or “when you come with your kingly power”, that is, at a future return as king. Some early manuscripts read “into your kingdom”, which favors the first sense. The English phrase chosen can carry either.

Greek manuscripts had no punctuation, so “today” could in principle go with “I tell you” (“Truly I tell you today, you will be with me”). Almost all translators and commentators take it with what follows, since the “Truly I tell you” formula never elsewhere carries a time word and the promise answers the man’s indefinite “when”.

The word, borrowed from Persian, meant an enclosed park or garden, and the Greek Old Testament uses it for the garden of Eden. In Jewish usage of the period it had come to name the place of blessedness where the righteous dead are with God.

Hours were counted from sunrise, so the sixth hour is about noon and the ninth hour about three in the afternoon. The word rendered “land” can also mean “earth”; the scope of the darkness is not specified.

The earliest manuscripts say the sun “failed” or “gave out”; many later ones read “the sun was darkened”. The verb was also the usual term for an eclipse, but it need not be technical here, and a solar eclipse cannot occur at the full moon of Passover.

Greek has one word for the whole temple complex with its courts and another, used here, for the building at its center where God was understood to dwell. Most English versions render both “temple”; “sanctuary” keeps the distinction. The curtain is most often taken to be the one that screened off the innermost room, though some think the curtain at the entrance of the building is meant.

The Greek adjective means both “righteous” and, in a legal setting, “innocent”, and many versions choose “innocent” here after Pilate’s three declarations that Jesus had done nothing deserving death. “Righteous” is kept because it includes innocence and matches the description of Joseph in verse 50. Greek uses one word-family where English has two; “justly” in verse 41 is the related adverb.

notes.phrase: the Sabbath was about to begin
notes.note: “Preparation” was the name for the day before the Sabbath, that is, Friday. The Sabbath began at sunset. The Greek verb literally means “was dawning” and is used here loosely for the start of the day, so the burial was carried out in the last hours of Friday afternoon.

candidates.reason: Recurs throughout the Gospels and Acts; “scribes” suggests copyists to a modern reader, and translators vary among “scribes”, “teachers of the law” and “legal experts”.
Numbered hours recur in all four Gospels and Acts, and the choice between keeping the ancient count and converting to “noon” or “three in the afternoon” must be uniform.
Used of Pilate’s beating here and of divine and parental discipline in Hebrews 12, 1 Corinthians 11 and Revelation 3; versions vary among chastise, punish, discipline and train.

Covers rescue from danger, healing and final salvation across the New Testament; the mockery here depends on the same word used elsewhere for healings, so a policy on “save”, “heal” and “rescue” is needed.
Used of Jewish council members, synagogue officials, civil magistrates and spiritual powers; versions vary among rulers, leaders, authorities and officials.
